title: Docs: refresh Security Overview + deployment boundary + audit logging pages (for Security Kit v2 links)
author: Wei Chen
release_notes: External docs referenced in Security FAQ/RFP responses updated to match Security Enablement Kit v2 terminology and Hosted/Dedicated/Private boundary descriptions.
description:
Summary
This PR refreshes a small set of public-facing docs pages that are referenced by the Enterprise Security FAQ v2 and the standard RFP response library. Goal is to ensure link targets and wording are consistent with the enablement kit while staying within what we can safely publish publicly (no restricted evidence, no over-commitments).

Context
Sales/SEs have been sending prospects links from the FAQ/RFP answers. Several of those pages were outdated or ambiguous (especially around deployment mode responsibility boundaries and audit log availability/export). This is a docs-only alignment pass; no product behavior changes.

What changed (high level)
- Security Overview page: clarified Redwood’s security program at a high level, added a clear “shared responsibility” section, and updated terminology to match the enablement kit (Hosted / Dedicated / Private).
- Deployment Modes / Security Boundary page: rewrote boundary language so it is explicit about control plane vs customer environment responsibilities, and removed absolute language (e.g., “never stores” / “always”).
- Audit Logging overview page: aligned event categories and availability statements to current reality; added guidance on what customers can expect to see in audit logs, and where audit logs live/are accessed depending on deployment mode.
- Link hygiene: updated internal cross-links and anchors used by the FAQ/RFP library so that the URLs are stable and less likely to break with minor nav changes.

Detailed changes
1) docs/security/overview.md
- Added “Deployment modes and responsibility boundaries” callout linking to boundary page.
- Added subsection “Evidence and reports” that explains the process at a high level (e.g., SOC 2 report availability under NDA) without exposing restricted instructions.
- Replaced ambiguous statements about data handling with mode-specific language (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private).

2) docs/security/deployment-modes.md
- Introduced a table: Hosted / Dedicated / Private with columns for “Compute environment”, “Network boundary”, “Customer-managed keys (optional)”, “Operational responsibility”.
- Explicitly called out that Private deployments can be in customer VPC and (where contracted) on-prem, and that operational responsibilities differ by deployment.
- Added short “What this page is / isn’t” disclaimer to avoid it being interpreted as contractual.

3) docs/security/audit-logging.md
- Clarified current audit log scope as “control-plane and administrative actions” and kept roadmap language out.
- Added examples of event categories (auth/admin, API key lifecycle, org/project changes) without listing full internal schema.
- Added “Export and integration” section: describes that customers can pull audit events via the Console/API (where available) and integrate with SIEM using standard log forwarding patterns; avoids committing to a specific vendor integration.

Files changed
- docs/security/overview.md
- docs/security/deployment-modes.md
- docs/security/audit-logging.md
- docs/security/_sidebar.yml
- docs/_redirects
- docs/security/_glossary.md
- docs/security/faq-links.md (new; internal doc in repo to centralize canonical link targets used in enablement content)

Illustrative snippet (deployment boundary table)
Hosted: Redwood-managed runtime and infrastructure; customer configures org/projects, access controls, and usage policies.
Dedicated: Redwood-managed dedicated capacity; customer gets stronger isolation and predictable throughput; responsibilities for identity/config still shared.
Private: Customer-managed network boundary; Redwood provides the platform components per deployment model; operational responsibility is defined by contract and deployment architecture.

Why this is safe to publish
- No restricted artifacts (SOC 2 report, pen test summary) are linked directly.
- No incident notification timelines are specified; language points to contractual terms and the support/security contact path.
- No “guarantees” are introduced; statements are bounded (e.g., “supported,” “available,” “by configuration,” “subject to contract”).

Testing
- Ran docs build locally (pnpm docs:build)
- Verified redirects and anchors for links referenced by enablement kit (manual check)
- CI: lint + link-check + build

Review notes / discussion
- Elliot Price (Docs): Requested we avoid “SIEM export” implying a one-click integration; updated wording to “integration using standard log forwarding patterns” and removed vendor examples.
- Naomi Feldman (Security & Compliance PM): Flagged that the previous Security Overview implied fixed incident notification windows; adjusted to contract-dependent language and referenced status page + support channels.
- Marcus Lin (Security Eng): Confirmed audit logging claims match current implementation; asked to avoid enumerating exact internal event names that are still in flux; replaced with category-level examples.
- Daniel Carter (GRC): Requested the “Evidence and reports” section explicitly state SOC 2 report sharing is under NDA and through the security review process; added a short sentence and removed any procedural detail.

Checklist
- [x] Terminology matches Security Enablement Kit v2 (Hosted/Dedicated/Private)
- [x] No restricted evidence linked
- [x] Avoids absolutes and non-contractual commitments
- [x] Links/anchors stable for RFP/FAQ references

Follow-ups
- PR #4863 will add a public-facing high-level Security FAQ page. This PR intentionally focuses on the core reference pages that RFP/FAQ answers link to today.
- If/when audit log export mechanisms change, we should update docs/security/faq-links.md first so enablement content can reference stable anchors.
